unique.reason: Real point: required name and tenancy plus a need-implying format still builds an identified need record; no route to public alternative formats without identity. Somewhat secondary to the disability field.
A missing commitment on provenance and fidelity of produced versions; reasonable but inferred, since no version is in the material. Small burden.
Statement gives no information on adapting via own device or assistive technology; a modest omission, close to generic advice.
Speculative; the reviewer admits the material cannot establish any disclosure. Data-collection concern for the assistant is already implicit in the AI claim.
Disability data shared with housing officer and tenancy file, notice placed after submit, no lawful basis or retention: a real privacy exposure.
Form collects no contact details or preferred reply channel/format; a promised reply may not reach the person usably.
Closed single-choice format list with no Other, missing formats (languages, accessible electronic documents) the page itself implies; real barrier.
Required tenancy reference whose hint points to a document the person may not be able to read; no route for advocates. Can block the request.
No custom error handling beyond native validation; real but partly generic, and native required validation is broadly accessible.
Free-text field lacks guidance on what to identify; small burden causing vague requests.
No standing preference for future letters; each letter arrives first in inaccessible form, a repeated real barrier.
No review or confirmation step after submission; minor burden, though weighting by AAA claim is beside the point.
Jargon (WCAG, AAA, conformant) unexplained for a tenant audience; minor comprehension burden.
46rem column gives roughly 85-90 character lines; real but minor reading burden.
No scope statement on what the claims cover; minor omission.
